answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so a node’s voting weight depends on paths from independently trusted sources, not merely on identities it creates. A sybil cluster S with few external edges has low conductance, φ(S)=cut(S,¬S)/vol(S); under volume-weighted trust, its probability of receiving outside trust is limited by this bottleneck. Thus its aggregate vote is bounded by boundary leakage, not its raw population—a narrow bridge may carry an ember plume, but cannot amplify it without limit.
